items.a: On the App Store for iPhone and iPad, and on Google Play for Android. <!--if WONDERWHY_PREMIUM-->It’s free to download.<!--else-->It’s free.<!--end-->

items.q: Which languages and editions are there?
items.a: The app is in English, Turkish, Spanish and German. There are five editions: Türkiye (Turkish), United States (English), World (English), Spain (Spanish) and Germany (German).

items.q: Who writes and reads the news?
items.a: AI writes the briefings from public news sources, and an AI voice reads them. Every story shows its sources. AI can make mistakes, so check the original when it matters.

items.q: Is it like a news podcast?
items.a: Like a news podcast made for you: a few minutes of news on the topics you pick, written and read by AI and updated through the day. Stop it anytime to ask a question.

items.aHtml: Your spoken question is sent to Google’s Gemini service so it can be understood and answered. We don’t store the recording. The question and answer are kept only if you report an answer (for 7 days) or when a “what is …?” question is saved to My questions in your Library (until you delete your account). The Privacy Policy has the details.

items.q: Where does the news come from?
items.a: From news outlets’ public feeds (RSS). The app groups stories that several outlets cover and shows where they differ.

<!--if WONDERWHY_PREMIUM-->It’s free to download, and you can listen for a set time every day for free. A Premium subscription unlocks features such as unlimited and offline listening<!--if WONDERWHY_ADS-->, with no ads<!--end-->; the App Store and Google Play show the price.<!--else-->No. The app is free right now.<!--if WONDERWHY_ADS--> It shows ads.<!--end--><!--end-->

items.q: Does it work with CarPlay and Android Auto?
items.a: <!--if WONDERWHY_PREMIUM-->Yes, with Premium. Start your briefing from the car’s screen and move between Today, My list and sections.<!--else-->Yes. Start your briefing from the car’s screen and move between Today, My list and sections.<!--end-->

<!--if WONDERWHY_VOICE_COMMANDS-->While you listen, say a short command like “stop”, “next” or “faster”. Commands work with headphones. Your phone’s own speech recognizer understands them; the audio isn’t sent anywhere.<!--end-->
<!--if WONDERWHY_PREMIUM-->Yes, with Premium. Download today’s stories to your phone and listen without a connection. Downloads are removed the next day.<!--end-->

items.q: <!--if WONDERWHY_PREMIUM-->How do I cancel my subscription?<!--end-->
items.aHtml: In your App Store or Google Play account. The steps are on the Support page.
See the Support page or write to {hello}.

support.lead: If you have a question, an idea or a problem, email us.
support.privacyHtml: To see, correct, export or delete your data, write to {privacy}. The Privacy Policy explains your rights.
support.deleteHtml: In the app, go to Profile › Delete account. This deletes your account, your synced data, your votes and your usage records at once. Without the app, write to {privacy}. The steps and what is kept are on the Delete your account page.
support.guestTitle: Only looked around without an account?
support.guestHtml: Deleting the app removes the lists and settings it kept on your phone. A guest ID the app may have created on our servers is deleted automatically after 7 days without use. To have it deleted sooner, write to {privacy}.
support.faqHtml: More answers are in the FAQ.
support.subscriptionHtml: Premium is managed and cancelled in your store account: on iPhone and iPad in Settings › your name › Subscriptions, on Android in the Play Store › profile › Payments & subscriptions › Subscriptions. After you cancel, Premium lasts until the end of the period. On a new phone, open Profile › Subscription in the app and tap Restore purchases. Refunds are handled by Apple or Google. Deleting your account doesn’t cancel the subscription. The full terms are in the Terms of Use.

compare.title: Compare news sources on the same story
compare.lead: One event, several outlets, different versions. Wonderwhy lines them up and shows you where they part ways, without opening five tabs.
compare.kindsTitle: What you see on every story

kinds.name: Conflicting
kinds.body: Numbers, dates or claims that don’t match between outlets.

kinds.name: Framed differently
kinds.body: The same fact, told with a clearly different emphasis.

kinds.name: Only one source
kinds.body: An important detail that only one outlet mentions.

kinds.name: Much the same
kinds.body: The outlets tell the story in much the same way.

compare.kindsNote: The label names the most serious difference found. It isn’t a score.

steps.title: Same event, grouped
steps.body: Reports of the same event from different outlets become one story in your edition: Türkiye, US, World, Spain or Germany.

steps.title: Compared by AI
steps.body: AI reads the reports side by side and sorts what differs. You see each source’s headline and the points where they part ways.

steps.title: Read the originals
steps.body: Tap any source to read its article. Think a comparison is wrong? Report it from the story.

compare.exampleLead: With made-up outlets, as in the app screen.

example.headline: Central bank keeps rates steady

sources.name: Harbor Daily
sources.title: Rates on hold as inflation cools

sources.name: Northline News
sources.title: Central bank keeps rates steady, eyes December

example.conflict: Northline News says the vote was unanimous; The Civic Ledger reports two members voted for a cut.
example.detail: Only Harbor Daily notes that mortgage rates barely moved.

limits: It doesn’t decide who is right. It shows where the reports differ; the call is yours.
It doesn’t rate outlets or their bias.
It can miss a difference. “Much the same” isn’t a guarantee.

faq.a: No. Wonderwhy doesn’t score outlets or label them left or right. It compares how the reports of one story differ: facts, framing and details.
The outlets in your edition’s news feeds: Turkish, American, Spanish, German and international. Every source is named and links to its original article.

faq.q: Can I listen to the story too?
faq.a: Yes. Every story is part of your short audio briefing. Hold the mic to ask about it, and the answer comes in the same voice.
